answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks through verifiable micro-additive manufacturing. Each node proves identity by actuating a capillary quill to print a conductive ridge on a substrate, verified via an electrical pulse. Attackers incur heavy capital costs maintaining robotic dispensers and consumable inks per identity rather than running virtual processes. However, particulate clogging inside the quill causes deposition flaws, occasionally rejecting authentic nodes.
